source: Copenhagen Burnout Inventory (CBI), first edition, February 2004, Borritz & Kristensen, National Research Centre for the Working Environment (NFA), Denmark.

personal.name: Personal Burnout
personal.definition: A state of prolonged physical and psychological exhaustion.

items.text: How often do you feel tired?
How often are you physically exhausted?
How often are you emotionally exhausted?
How often do you think: 'I can't take it anymore'?
How often do you feel worn out?
How often do you feel weak and susceptible to illness?

work.name: Work-related Burnout
work.definition: Prolonged physical and psychological exhaustion perceived as related to the person's work.

items.text: Do you feel burnt out because of your work?
Do you feel worn out at the end of the working day?
Are you exhausted in the morning at the thought of another day at work?
Do you feel that every working hour is tiring for you?
Do you have enough energy for family and friends during leisure time?

client.name: Client-related Burnout
client.definition: Prolonged physical and psychological exhaustion perceived as related to work with clients.

items.text: Do you find it hard to work with clients?
Do you find it frustrating to work with clients?
Does it drain your energy to work with clients?
Do you feel that you give more than you get back when you work with clients?
Are you tired of working with clients?
Do you sometimes wonder how long you will be able to continue working with clients?

supplementary_items.text: How heavy has your workload felt over the past two weeks? (supplementary, not validated)
How well do you feel you are recovering and sleeping outside of work? (supplementary, not validated)
Do you receive adequate support from your manager and peers when needed? (supplementary, not validated)
Do you feel you have control over how you organize your daily work tasks? (supplementary, not validated)
Overall, how satisfied are you with your work situation? (supplementary, not validated)
